title: Hackers reportedly breached an open-source intelligence platform used by US agencies, relayed from the New York Times
date_note: The relaying pages give only the day of the New York Times report, 24 November.
geo_basis: United States, where the agencies are based
summary: RBC Ukraine, citing the New York Times, says an open-source intelligence platform used by the CIA, ODNI and NGA may have been hit; it says agencies state secret networks were not harmed and it is fixed. RBC says early signs point to Chinese involvement, but the attackers are not identified. Tin Tuc, relaying the Times via RT, says two sources suggest Beijing and cite the AI tool Artex; VTC News names Artex but not China.
plain: RBC Ukraine, citing the New York Times, says a US intelligence open-source analysis platform may have been breached. Officials say secret networks were not affected and it is fixed.
exec: Per the New York Times as relayed by RBC Ukraine, a platform used by US intelligence agencies may have been breached; officials say secret networks were unaffected.

sources.name: RBC Ukraine (relaying the New York Times)
Tin Tuc (Vietnam), relaying the New York Times via RT
VTC News (via baomoi.com), relaying the New York Times

validation.note: Two Ukrainian publishers read (RBC Ukraine, 112 Ukraine), both relaying the New York Times / Bloomberg reporting, which was not read (the NYT page was not found; searches returned nothing). No US agency statement was read. Tin Tuc and VTC News (read 26 Nov) also relay the Times and say the agencies had not commented; still one original report.

review.note: stronger than the source: summary said VTC News relayed Beijing suggestion (VTC does not mention China; Tin Tuc does); agencies' statement attributed to RBC
